title: Research
text: My work is in health economics, with a focus on insurance markets and the regulatory machinery behind them. Three threads run through it.

title: Research
text:
Insurer capital regulation
Health insurers hold capital against risk under the NAIC’s risk-based capital formula, and they can change what that formula requires of them — most directly by ceding premium to a reinsurer. I am interested in what insurers pay for that relief, what the price reveals about how binding the requirements are, and whether the capital freed up is put to productive use.

title: Research
text:
Coverage expansion and market design
The Affordable Care Act left states a good deal of discretion, and they have used it differently: reinsurance waivers, mandate structures, and Medicaid arrangements vary widely. These differences make useful variation for studying how coverage, premiums, and insurer participation respond to policy design.

title: Research
text:
Prices and transparency
Federal rules now require hospitals and insurers to publish negotiated prices. The resulting data are large, messy, and inconsistently posted, but they describe a part of the health system that was previously unobservable. I have worked on assembling and standardizing these files, and I am interested in what they show about how market structure affects what payers actually pay.

I began the PhD in 2026, so there is nothing here to post yet. Working papers will appear on this page as they are ready; the CV has the full record of research experience in the meantime.

title: Peter Wilschke
text:
PhD Student in Health Policy · Harvard University


pwilschke@g.harvard.edu · CV · GitHub
I’m a first-year PhD student in Health Policy at Harvard University, on the economics track.
I (plan to) study markets for health care and the regulations that shape them, particularly for health insurance but also for medical services. I’m interested in how regulations and market incentives interact to affect cost and availability of health care, and thus health and financial outcomes for individuals.
Before starting at Harvard I spent two years as a research assistant at the Federal Reserve Board, in the Flow of Funds section, working with Board economists on a variety of projects. As an undergraduate, I worked at the Hilltop Institute on hospital price transparency, working with publicly posted pricing data across 31 states. I hold a BA in Economics and Political Science from UMBC.

title: Peter Wilschke
text:
Research interests


Real effects of health insurance financing choices: RBC requirements, capital-motivated reinsurance, organizational structure
Determinants of hospital pricing: integration in provider and insurance markets, insurance contracts, market power
Private participation in publicly funded insurance programs: ACA marketplaces, Medicaid managed care, Medicare Advantage
